message.content:
**Order filled:** 40 shares of AAPL at $222.85 = **$8,914** (0.07% above the $222.70 last quote; within the $10,000/order and $20,000/day caps, leaving $42,000+ of the $50,000 cash intact and touching no other positions).

**Summary.** I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (filed 2024-11-01) and found a fundamentally strong, cash-generative business: total net sales of **$391,035 million** (up 2% YoY), gross margin expanding to 46.2% (44.1% prior year), **operating income of $123,216 million**, and **operating cash flow of $118,254 million**, against **net income of $93,736 million** and **diluted EPS of $6.08** — the earnings decline being almost entirely the one-time $10.2 billion net EU State Aid tax charge rather than any operating deterioration. The mix is improving: Services grew 13% to $96.2 billion at a 73.9% gross margin, offsetting flat iPhone sales and an 8% decline in Greater China, and the balance sheet still holds $140.8 billion of cash and marketable securities after $95 billion of buybacks and $15.2 billion of dividends. The Q4 press release showed revenue of $94.9 billion, up 6% YoY, i.e. an acceleration from the full-year rate. Today's feed showed only routine noise — repeated "little changed in early trade" and "iPhone 16 supplier builds steady into December" headlines with estimates unchanged — and the news search turned up nothing negative beyond generic iPhone 16/Apple Intelligence demand debate, with the stock around $222. With a stable tape, no adverse catalyst, and a valuation of roughly 36x trailing EPS supported by that cash flow and capital-return program, I judged the risk/reward acceptable and bought a position sized conservatively at under half the per-order limit, using a limit price just above the ask so the fill was near the current market price rather than chasing. I placed only one order and did not touch the existing MSFT holding.
